title: O que está acontecendo na cena?
grammarPoint: Present continuous; present simple vs continuous

text.title: Scene 12: The Surprise Party
paragraphs: It is Friday evening in a small apartment in Los Angeles. Five friends are [[getting ready]] for a surprise party. Today is Tom's birthday, but he doesn't know about the party.

Right now, Jess is putting balloons in the living room. Her brother Leo is standing on a chair, and he is holding a big [[sign]] that says "Happy Birthday, Tom!" Priya is in the kitchen. She isn't cooking. She is [[ordering]] pizza on her phone.
Suddenly, someone is [[knocking]] at the door. Everybody is [[whispering]]: "Is it Tom? Is he coming in?" Leo is trying to get down from the chair, but the chair is moving.
Jess is walking to the door. She is opening it slowly. It isn't Tom. It's the pizza [[delivery guy]]! Now everybody is laughing. Tom usually gets home at eight, so they still have twenty minutes.

ordering.note: to order = pedir (comida, num restaurante ou app)

knocking.note: to knock at the door = bater na porta

grammar.title: Present continuous: o que está acontecendo agora
explanation: Usamos o present continuous para ações que estão acontecendo agora, neste momento. Ele combina com palavras como now, right now e at the moment.
A forma é am, is ou are + o verbo com -ing: I am working, she is cooking, they are waiting. Na fala, usamos muito as contrações: I'm, she's, they're.

Atenção à ortografia do -ing: verbos que terminam em -e perdem o e (make → making, move → moving). Verbos curtos que terminam em consoante + vogal + consoante dobram a última letra (sit → sitting, get → getting).
Na negativa, usamos isn't, aren't ou 'm not: she isn't cooking. Na pergunta, am, is ou are vêm antes do sujeito: Is he coming in?

Compare com o present simple, que fala de rotina e hábito: Tom usually gets home at eight (todo dia) e Now everybody is laughing (agora). Alguns verbos de estado, como know, like e want, normalmente não vão para o -ing: he doesn't know, e não he isn't knowing.

examples.en: Five friends are getting ready for a party.
examples.pt: Cinco amigos estão se preparando para uma festa.

examples.en: Tom usually gets home at eight.
examples.pt: O Tom normalmente chega em casa às oito.

exercises.explanation: O texto diz: "Priya is in the kitchen."
Falso: "She isn't cooking. She is ordering pizza on her phone."
Não é o Tom: "It's the pizza delivery guy!"
Falso: é uma festa surpresa, e o texto diz "he doesn't know about the party".

exercises.sentence: Right now, Leo ___ on a chair.
exercises.explanation: Ação acontecendo agora (right now): is + standing.

exercises.sentence: Look! The cat is ___ on the sofa.
exercises.explanation: Sit termina em consoante + vogal + consoante, então dobramos o t: sitting.
Usually indica rotina, então usamos o present simple. Com he (Tom): gets.

exercises.prompt: Qual frase descreve uma ação que está acontecendo agora?
exercises.explanation: Para algo acontecendo agora: is + ordering. Sem o is, a frase fica incorreta.

exercises.prompt: Coloque as palavras na ordem certa.
exercises.explanation: Na pergunta, is vem antes do sujeito: Is he coming in?
